items.news_title: Sam Altman got exceptionally testy over Claude Super Bowl ads
items.news_summary: AI company Anthropic aired Super Bowl ads mocking competitor OpenAI's plan to show ads in ChatGPT, leading to a heated response from OpenAI's CEO.

comic.panel_description: Split panel showing two chatbots as office workers. Left side: pristine, organized desk with halo. Right side: same desk covered in advertising billboards, popup ads, and sales flyers, with devil horns on the bot.
comic.caption: When AI assistants become advertising assistants
comic.image_prompt: RK Laxman style black ink line art showing two contrasting office cubicles, simple clean lines, minimal shading, exaggerated expressions, cluttered vs clean desks, newspaper comic aesthetic, common man watching from corner
comic.negative_prompt: specific company logos, real people, Sam Altman, ChatGPT interface, computer screens, corporate branding, photo-realism
comic.layout_notes: Caption centered below split panel, common man observer in bottom right corner, contrast between clean left and cluttered right sides

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon satirizes the tension between AI companies over advertising integration. By showing the same chatbot assistant in two states - one pure and one corrupted by ads - it highlights fears about commercialization degrading AI services. The common man's bewildered expression represents public confusion over competing AI claims.

safety_checks.notes: Avoids specific companies/individuals, uses generic office setting and characters

items.news_title: Concerned that FTA may cut access to medicines in India, rest of the developing world: Médecins Sans Frontières writes to EU
items.news_source: India Latest News: Top National Headlines Today & Breaking News | The Hindu
items.news_summary: Medical aid group MSF warns that EU-India trade deal could restrict access to affordable generic medicines in developing nations, potentially affecting millions dependent on Indian-made drugs.

comic.panel_description: Split panel showing two contrasting scenes: Left side shows a giant EU bureaucrat with a pen blocking medicine bottles from flowing through a door marked 'India'. Right side shows thin, worried patients in developing nations looking at empty medicine shelves.
comic.caption: When free trade agreements aren't so free after all...
comic.image_prompt: Editorial cartoon in RK Laxman style, black ink line art with minimal watercolor, showing oversized bureaucrat figure in suit blocking medicine flow, common people waiting anxiously, medicine bottles, traditional Indian architectural elements, newspaper texture background
comic.negative_prompt: avoid specific politicians, corporate logos, brand names, medical symbols, graphic illness, specific drug names, religious symbols
comic.layout_notes: Caption centered below split panel, bureaucrat figure dominates left panel, smaller worried figures clustered on right, medicine bottles as connecting visual element

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon illustrates the irony of how 'free' trade agreements can actually restrict access to essential goods. By showing a bureaucrat blocking medicine flow, it highlights how regulations in trade deals can harm vulnerable populations. The contrast between the powerful EU figure and desperate patients emphasizes the human cost of trade policies.

safety_checks.notes: Avoids naming specific companies or individuals. Uses metaphorical representation rather than direct criticism.

items.news_title: How Anthropic move is just a trailer of AI-pocalypse
items.news_summary: Anthropic's new AI automation tool causes panic in tech stocks as markets realize AI could replace IT services rather than just enhance them. The 'SaaSpocalypse' particularly impacts Indian IT companies.

comic.panel_description: A giant robot wearing a tie sits at an office desk, casually typing on multiple computers while sweating human IT workers peek nervously from behind cubicle walls. The robot has a name tag reading 'AI'. In the corner, a stock market display shows falling numbers.
comic.caption: "Don't worry, I'm just here to enhance your productivity!"
comic.image_prompt: Editorial cartoon style, black ink line art with minimal color, showing comical office scene with large mechanical robot in business attire, nervous office workers hiding, cubicle office setting, stock market display board, RK Laxman style cross-hatching, simple clean lines, exaggerated expressions
comic.negative_prompt: realistic faces, company logos, specific tech brands, photorealistic style, gore, violence, corporate logos, named individuals
comic.layout_notes: Caption below panel, stock ticker display visible in upper right corner, emphasize size contrast between robot and hiding workers

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon satirizes the tech industry's previous notion that AI would merely enhance existing business models rather than replace them entirely. The irony is captured in the robot's reassuring statement while clearly taking over the workplace. The nervous workers represent the IT sector's growing realization that AI might eliminate rather than augment their roles.

safety_checks.notes: Generic representation of AI impact on workforce, no specific companies or individuals targeted

items.news_title: Fergus O'Neill moves to Sydney Sixers amid talk over Victoria future
items.news_summary: Cricket bowler switches teams from Melbourne to Sydney amid speculation about state loyalty. His career move highlights tension between state teams competing for talent.

comic.panel_description: A confused cricket bowler stands at a crossroads with multiple road signs pointing to different cities. He juggles cricket balls while wearing half a Sydney uniform and half a Melbourne uniform. A kangaroo in the background holds a contract and looks amused.
comic.caption: When bowling down the middle means playing both sides
comic.image_prompt: Indian editorial cartoon style, black ink line art, cricket bowler at crossroads, split uniform, confused expression, exaggerated road signs, amused kangaroo in business suit, cricket balls in air, RK Laxman style hatching, minimal watercolor wash, sepia tones
comic.negative_prompt: real cricketers, team logos, actual uniforms, photo-realistic faces, cricket grounds, brand names, aggressive poses
comic.layout_notes: Caption below image, road signs readable but generic, central figure prominent, kangaroo in lower right corner as observing character

items.explanation_paragraph: The cartoon satirizes the increasingly fluid nature of player loyalty in modern cricket, where state boundaries become blurred by commercial interests. The split uniform visualizes the identity crisis faced by players caught between different teams and opportunities. The amused kangaroo represents the Australian cricket establishment watching talent hop between states.

safety_checks.notes: Generic representation avoids specific player likeness. No controversial elements present.
